value.body: A public affairs associate helps a company, industry body or non-profit follow government policy and engage with it. Public affairs consultancies, industry associations, companies and advocacy groups hire them. A typical day involves tracking new rules, summarising what they mean, and preparing notes for meetings or consultations.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA in Political Science, Economics or Law-related studies

items.label: Common sources
items.value: Gazette notifications, parliamentary records, ministry consultations

items.label: Postgraduate students in political science
items.note: PG enrolment; one common background for policy work
items.source: AISHE (Ministry of Education) 2023-24, Table 13 (based on actual responses)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start as an associate or analyst at a public affairs or policy consultancy, or in the policy team of an industry body. Internships with legislators, think tanks or advocacy groups are a common way in.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading bills, rules and government notifications

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: public policy manager, government relations lead, policy consultant.
Work clusters around Delhi and state capitals.
Some move on to a master's in public policy for senior roles.

competition.note: BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
